stories.title: Advocates say Canada is 'turning its back' on holding companies accountable for rights violations
stories.summary: Human-rights advocates say Ottawa is betraying foreign complainants who allege involvement by Canadian companies in forced labour and environmental degradation abroad, by shutting down the office meant to probe those reports. This is the on-the-ground advocacy reaction to the elimination of the Canadian Ombudsperson for Responsible Enterprise (CORE) flagged in brief_20260619 -- removing the only dedicated federal channel scrutinizing the overseas conduct of Canadian mining, garment, and oil-and-gas firms.
stories.connection: DIRECTLY on-mission oversight-dismantlement thread, continuing from brief_20260619. CORE's remit (Canadian companies operating abroad) overlaps the arms-export accountability work in arms_exports_israel.json and arms_pipeline_dossier.json, and the corporate-structure mapping in business_holdings_dossier.json -- defence/extractive firms exporting or operating overseas lose an independent complaints channel. Pairs with the Bill C-30 item below as a two-item 'oversight bypass' cluster. Recommend an 'oversight_dismantlement' tracker cross-referencing officer_of_parliament_findings.json and csis_oversight_accountability_dossier.json.

stories.title: Pesticide law granting cabinet power to authorize products Health Canada deemed unsafe is now in force
stories.summary: The federal government has enacted major changes to pesticide regulation, granting cabinet the power to authorize the use of pesticides -- including ones Health Canada has assessed as unsafe. The measure (Bill C-30, passed before Parliament rose) bypassed committee study and scientific/public-health testimony. The health minister's office framed the powers around 'successful harvests' and 'food sovereignty'; the NDP and Green Party condemned the lack of scrutiny.
stories.connection: NEW governance / rule-of-law-process thread now confirmed in force: cabinet assumes a discretionary power to override a regulator's safety determination with Parliamentary scrutiny bypassed -- the regulatory-capture vs. independent-enforcement pattern tracked in financial_crime_policy_2026.json and procurement_anomalies.json, and adjacent to the health-lobbying mapping in maid_health_lobbyists.json. Flag for a health/regulatory-accountability watch entry.

stories.title: Grassy Narrows woman with mercury poisoning demands Carney apologize for 'outlast' remark
stories.summary: A Grassy Narrows First Nation woman who suffers from mercury poisoning is adamant that Prime Minister Mark Carney must apologize for saying he could 'outlast' her during a March protest, and is demanding action on the decades-old mercury contamination. The story couples a sitting PM's dismissive remark with an unresolved Indigenous environmental-health crisis.
stories.connection: Logs to indigenous_accountability_dossier.json and indigenous_grover_decisionmakers.json -- Crown conduct toward an Indigenous claimant plus an unremediated environmental-health harm. Adjacent to the opioid/health harm framing in opioid_crisis_accountability_dossier.json (state duty-of-care to a harmed population). Carry forward as a Crown-Indigenous accountability signal with a named decision-maker (the PM).

stories.title: Poilievre and Conservative MPs announce they will oppose ratifying the K'omoks First Nation treaty
stories.summary: Federal Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre announced that he and other Conservative MPs will oppose ratification of the K'omoks First Nation's treaty; the K'omoks chief pushed back publicly. The move injects partisan opposition into a modern-treaty ratification process on Vancouver Island.
stories.connection: Indigenous-accountability / Crown-Indigenous file (indigenous_accountability_dossier.json). Lower direct investigative weight than the mercury or corporate-oversight items, but logged as a federal-political-opposition data point on modern-treaty ratification -- relevant context for how the accountability narrative intersects party positioning. Cross-reference osint_mp_dossiers.json for the MPs taking the position.

stories.title: Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami warns it may seek foreign partners if Ottawa keeps 'colonial' Arctic policy
stories.summary: After a two-day Arctic sovereignty conference in Ottawa, Canada's national Inuit organization (ITK) is calling on the federal government to be a better partner, rejecting 'outdated, colonial approaches to Arctic policy,' and signalling it could pursue foreign partners if the relationship sours. The statement links Indigenous self-determination to national Arctic-sovereignty and foreign-policy stakes.
stories.connection: Sits at the intersection of indigenous_accountability_dossier.json and the foreign-influence/sovereignty material in foreign_interference_dossier.json -- an Indigenous national organization explicitly raising the prospect of foreign partnerships frames a Crown-relations failure with national-security adjacency. Carry forward as a watch item on Arctic governance and Crown-Inuit relations.

stories.title: Ottawa adds $5.4B over two years to sustain the national $10-a-day child-care program
stories.summary: The federal government is giving provinces and territories an additional $5.4 billion over two years for the national $10-a-day child-care program to address 'cost pressures' on fees, staffing, and capacity, families minister Patty Hajdu said. A large mid-program federal top-up to a flagship transfer.
stories.connection: Federal-transfer spending data point relevant to procurement_anomalies.json and financial_transaction_analysis.json as a macro public-spending backdrop. Low direct investigative weight, but a multi-billion-dollar transfer top-up is worth logging for spending-trajectory context against the technical-recession framing carried from brief_20260619.
